title: Ledger-anchor checkpoints for cross-region reconnect de-duplication
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Background: Intermittent reconnects during cross-region failover can cause duplicate token accounting when clients resume streaming sessions against a different backend. Current session-resume semantics rely on best-effort idempotency tokens but do not provide a tamper-evident reconciliation anchor that survives region failover and partial replication delays. This ticket introduces a ledger-anchor checkpoint protocol to guarantee at-most-once finalization of token credits across regions and to make reconcilers provably idempotent.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a compact ledger-anchor checkpoint blob that is emitted at session finalization and periodically for long-lived streams
Backend accepts resume requests only when client presents a matching checkpoint proof OR uses deterministic merge logic that avoids double-crediting
Cross-region handoff path validates anchors within 5 seconds of failover under simulated 250ms inter-region replication lag
End-to-end integration test shows zero duplicate billing when simulating reconnects and model-switch fallback during active streams
Observability: new metrics for anchor-emission-rate, anchor-verify-latency, and anchor-reconcile-mismatches exposed in console dashboard
implementation_notes: Design: emit a signed checkpoint (anchor) containing session-id, last-output-offset, cumulative-input-tokens, cumulative-output-tokens, and a monotonically increasing sequence. Anchors are published to a regional durable topic and compacted into a ledger entry. On reconnect, the new region attempts to fetch the latest anchor for the session; if found, it uses the anchor to reconcile credits (fast path). If not found within a configurable window, fall back to deterministic merge heuristics with provisional credits and a follow-up reconciliation job.
